summary: @servicetitan/dte-unlayer 0.150.4 preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads a platform-specific Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts and chmods the Bun binary, and then uses it to execute a sibling file math_init.js from the tarball root. math_init.js is a ~727 KB heavily obfuscated blob using string-array rotation (function WV8StW) with a permuted-alphabet character decoder (hc1jfK9) and hex-mangled identifiers, unrelated to the package's advertised purpose as an Unlayer email-editor React wrapper. The library's dist/ and src/ trees implement the Unlayer wrapper normally and do not reference setup.mjs or math_init.js; the malicious surface is confined to the install lifecycle and never touches consumers who only require() the library. Using a downloaded alternate JavaScript runtime (Bun) to execute an obfuscated payload at npm install time is an evasion technique against Node-based install inspection, and running an opaque 727 KB blob with the installer's privileges yields arbitrary code execution on the developer/build machine. The @servicetitan scope suggests a hijack or malicious release published under an otherwise legitimate namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
